title: Training intensity distribution analysis by race pace vs. physiological approach in world-class middle- and long-distance runners
authors: Kenneally M, Casado A, Gomez-Ezeiza J, Santos-Concejero J
population: Seven world-class middle- and long-distance runners, 50 weeks of training
findings: Race-pace zones gave 88.5/7.4/4.1% in Z1/Z2/Z3; physiological zones gave 87.2/6.1/6.6%; differences in Z2 (ES=1.20, large) and Z3 (ES=0.93, moderate).

Race-pace zones produced pyramidal TID in all phases; physiological zones produced polarized or pyramidal depending on season phase in middle-distance runners and pyramidal throughout in long-distance runners.
limitations: Seven world-class runners, descriptive; neither anchor was shown to be superior.
implications: Whether a plan is labelled polarized or pyramidal depends on the zone anchor, so report TID with both physiological (LT1/LT2) and race-pace anchors.
Define race-specific sessions relative to goal race pace and easy/moderate classification relative to physiological thresholds; name the anchor whenever a TID label is shown.

verification.notes: Crossref: online 2020-06-20, print 2021-06. All numbers confirmed in abstract.
